tagline: From an Ohio River wharf to a minister's six-sided study.
intro: Wellsburg sits on the Ohio River, and Patrick Gass, the last surviving member of the Lewis and Clark expedition, made his home there. The loop's other end is Bethany, where Alexander Campbell founded a college in 1840 and platted the town seven years later.

Between them, Fowlerstown grew up along the Washington Pike around William Fowler's grist mill. Campbell's house outside Bethany kept growing too, with rooms added for his seminary students and for his regular parade of visitors.

moments.title: Wellsburg Wharf
moments.text: Cobblestones along the riverbank and the foundations of two warehouses are what remain of the public wharf built in 1836.

moments.title: Fowlerstown
moments.text: The brick Greek Revival inn, built between 1848 and 1851, housed the village's general store and post office before 1938.

moments.title: Alexander Campbell Mansion
moments.text: Near the much-enlarged house, where Campbell married Margaret Brown in the parlor in 1811, stands the small hexagonal stone building he used as library and office.
